# M10.2 — Allocator-safe physical memory reservations

Date: 2026-11-25 (Asia/Kolkata)  
Result: **PASS for the supported single-BSP Limine/Q35 configuration**. No page allocator was implemented.

## Architecture and ownership

The engine accepts half-open physical intervals `[base,end)`, rounds protected starts down and ends up, sorts and merges adjacent or overlapping intervals, then subtracts their union from usable 4 KiB pages. It retains every original interval and reason for provenance. Arithmetic and capacities are checked; failures halt before any allocator-safe marker. The result remains static, read-only kernel storage.

The installed [Limine protocol](https://github.com/limine-bootloader/limine-protocol/blob/trunk/PROTOCOL.md) states that usable entries contain no valuable data, the handoff stack, responses and associated data, and bootloader page tables live in bootloader-reclaimable memory, and the executable has a uniform virtual-to-physical offset. The protocol also permits nonusable entries to overlap one another; M10.1's validator was corrected accordingly. The installed header supplies the actual response layouts and type constants. [Intel's SDM](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/intel-sdm.html) describes CR0.PG, CR4.PAE/LA57, EFER.LMA, CR3, and the four-level entry format.

Only `LIMINE_MEMMAP_USABLE` contributes eligible pages. Every nonusable region, including bootloader-reclaimable, ACPI, bad, firmware, framebuffer, unknown, and executable/modules, is explicitly protected. Page zero, kernel image including BSS, framebuffer extent, and every reachable active page-table frame are additionally recorded. Overlapping reasons do not double-count pages.

## Kernel, stack, responses, and page tables

The Limine executable-address response and linker `__kernel_end` establish the entire loaded kernel image, including BSS and reservation-engine storage. The runtime checks its physical extent is inside a kernel/modules map entry, and checks that the active GDT/TSS, IDT and three 16 KiB IST stacks are inside that extent. The handoff RSP is checked inside a bootloader-reclaimable interval. Its precise allocated stack bounds remain unknown; the *entire* containing bootloader-reclaimable interval is excluded, as required by Limine's stack ownership guarantee. No stack switch was added.

The walker reads CR3 and verifies CR0.PG, CR4.PAE, CR4.LA57=0, and EFER.LMA. It resolves a table page through HHDM only after proving the whole page lies in a bootloader-reclaimable region, which Limine guarantees for its active tables. It visits present non-leaf PML4/PDPT/PD/PT entries, counts 1 GiB and 2 MiB leaves without descending into them, deduplicates shared frames, rejects a frame reused at different levels, and fails closed at 4,096 frames or on malformed/inaccessible entries. It never writes page tables. Framebuffer pitch×height is overflow checked and its physical range is matched against a framebuffer map entry. Every used Limine response, map pointer array and map entry object is checked in bootloader-reclaimable memory. The protocol conservatively covers any associated response data not individually enumerated.

## Runtime results

| RAM | Accelerator | Raw usable bytes | Original candidates | Unique excluded | Final eligible pages | Eligible bytes | Ranges | Table frames PML4/PDPT/PD/PT |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 256 MiB | KVM | 221417472 | 54057 | 1 | 54056 | 221413376 | 9 | 1/2/3/4 |
| 512 MiB | KVM | 489852928 | 119593 | 1 | 119592 | 489848832 | 9 | 1/2/3/4 |
| 1024 MiB | KVM | 1026723840 | 250665 | 1 | 250664 | 1026719744 | 9 | 1/2/3/4 |
| 256 MiB | TCG | 221417472 | 54057 | 1 | 54056 | 221413376 | 9 | 1/2/3/4 |

Every VM reached `ALLOCATOR-SAFE INVENTORY: PASS`, `PHYSICAL MEMORY ALLOCATOR: NOT INITIALIZED`, and `M10.2 COMPLETE`. The independent runner parsed all memory-map and protected intervals, merged them itself, reconstructed exact eligible intervals and counts, verified no protected overlap, checked all reported table frames were protected, and compared CPU descriptor state with QEMU's monitor. CPL=0, IF=0, HLT=1; final RIP was `0xFFFFFFFF80003282` after the checkpoint HLT. No unexpected exception or reset occurred. The TCG evidence includes QEMU physical `xp` inspection of active PML4 entries at CR3, matching reported child table frames. Saved transcripts, monitor registers, mapping output, root-table dump, emulator logs, screenshots and result JSON are under each run directory.

Actual graphical screenshot: `build/m10-memory-reservations/run-8t2i7_x0/screen.png` (1280×800). The on-screen M10.2 count is calculated at runtime.

## Complete reservation provenance and eligible intervals

Reason codes: 1 page zero; 2 nonusable map; 3 kernel; 4 descriptors; 5 IST stacks; 6 conservative containing stack region; 7 page-table frame; 8 Limine response objects; 9 framebuffer; 10 engine storage. Descriptor, IST and engine objects also lie within reason-3 kernel image. The normal stack and responses also lie within reason-2 bootloader-reclaimable regions. Exact objects and conservative containing intervals are deliberately distinguished. Lines below preserve all intervals, including overlapping provenance; the subtraction algorithm merges them first.

## Host tests, build, and bugs

- Previous M09: **942/942** normal and **942/942** ASan/UBSan.
- M10.1 map validator: **32/32** normal and **32/32** ASan/UBSan, including the corrected nonusable overlap rule.
- M10.2 reservation and table tests: **6,682/6,682** normal and **6,682/6,682** ASan/UBSan. These include 200 deterministic random interval trials checked against a per-page reference model, capacity exhaustion, shared tables, large leaves, malformed entries, recursion, and traversal-limit failure. Total **7,656/7,656** in each mode. LeakSanitizer was disabled in the inherited sandbox runner; AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer ran.
- ELF audit: three expected load segments, `kernel_main` entry at `0xFFFFFFFF80001000`, permanent tables and fatal stubs, required memory symbols, no unresolved symbols, no STI, and expected descriptor activation instruction order. Freestanding GCC used `-Wall -Wextra -Werror`.
- Clean scratch copy excluding `.git`, `build`, and `dist` produced byte-identical ELF and ISO.
- Initial host fixture accidentally omitted the present bit from a malformed PML4 test; fixed the fixture. The QEMU runner was extended to parse the new terminal marker and independently reconstruct every eligible interval. The M10.1 overlap validator was corrected after reading the installed protocol guarantee.

## Files

Created `kernel/memory_reservations.c`, `kernel/include/memory_reservations.h`, `kernel/page_table_inventory.c`, `kernel/include/page_table_inventory.h`, `tests/memory_reservations_test.c`, `experiments/m10-memory-reservations/main.c`, `experiments/m10-memory-reservations/limine.conf`, `experiments/m10-memory-reservations/linker.ld`, `scripts/build-m10-memory-reservations.sh`, `scripts/check-m10-reservations-elf.py`, `scripts/test-m10-reservations-host.sh`, and `scripts/test-m10-memory-reservations.py`. Modified M10.1's map validator, test and report to follow the actual protocol's nonusable-overlap rule. No stable M09 source was changed.

## Limits and M10.3 readiness

The supported guarantee is the tested single-BSP Limine base-revision-6 four-level boot contract. Exact handoff-stack allocation bounds are unresolved, but its entire containing bootloader-reclaimable region is excluded. The active table tree is inventoried read-only; no allocator may reclaim bootloader memory or switch paging based solely on this milestone. M10.3 may implement a bitmap allocator *only* over these validated eligible ranges, initialize all metadata in already reserved kernel storage or explicitly reserve its backing pages first, and test allocation/free invariants without enabling interrupts or reclaiming firmware memory.

## Interview questions

1. **Why half-open intervals?** `[base,end)` gives length `end-base` and makes adjacent ranges unambiguous.
2. **Why round reservations outward?** Any page touched by a protected byte must be withheld.
3. **Why round usable ranges inward?** Partly usable pages cannot be safely allocated whole.
4. **Why merge before subtraction?** Overlapping reservations must exclude each page once.
5. **Why retain original reasons?** A merged interval otherwise loses evidence of who owns it.
6. **Why not subtract HHDM from every pointer?** Kernel image pointers use an independent executable mapping.
7. **How is the normal stack protected without exact bounds?** Limine owns its backing in bootloader-reclaimable memory, and all such memory is excluded.
8. **What is a large-page leaf?** A PDPT or PD entry that maps data directly, with no child table to traverse.
9. **What does CR3 provide?** The physical root table frame, not the whole tree.
10. **What must an allocator do next?** Manage only verified eligible frames and reserve its own metadata before use.
